chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who became junub and then performed ghusl before urinating, then something came out of him. He said: He repeats the ghusl. I said: What about the woman, from whom something comes out after ghusl? He said: She does not repeat. I said: What is the difference between them? He said: Because what comes out of the woman is only the man's fluid.

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْفَرْقُ: the legal distinction between the two cases
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, whose ruling is contrasted with the man
key_terms.مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ: the man's fluid, which explains the ruling in context
key_terms.يَبُولَ: to urinate, mentioned here as istibra' before ghusl

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to repeat ghusl if fluid comes out after ghusl al-janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on ghusl after janabah when discharge exits after bathing. It distinguishes between the man and the woman in this case, explaining that the woman's post-ghusl discharge is regarded as the man's fluid and therefore does not require repeating the ghusl.
